title: Beyond Components: Designing Generative UI for MCP Apps — Ruben Casas, Postman
talk_summary: A Postman engineer surveys three tiers of generative UI (static components, declarative JSON/YAML descriptors, and fully LLM-generated HTML/CSS/JS) and argues MCP apps' sandboxed double-iFrame delivery is the right containment boundary for agent-generated UI. The talk is mostly forward-looking UI design speculation, but it contains a few transferable mechanisms around sandboxing untrusted generated code and using declarative descriptors to constrain model output.

takeaways.technique: Sandbox all model-generated code before execution/display
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats LLM-generated HTML/CSS/JS as untrusted third-party code and requires containment via MCP apps' default double-iFrame sandbox before presenting it to users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we don't trust third-party code, well, we should not trust um, code that has been generated by LLMs

takeaways.technique: Declarative descriptor instead of free-form code generation
takeaways.evidence_quote: The LLM is not generating these components. The LLM is generating the JSON.

takeaways.technique: Cheaper tier for structured output, expensive tier only when needed
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues declarative UI is 'faster and also potentially cheaper' because the model emits a small descriptor rather than full code, reserving full codegen for cases that need it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: also faster and also potentially cheaper at this point. Uh, so you don't create and use a lot of tokens

takeaways.technique: Constrained output schema for reviewer verdicts
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses a descriptor/translation layer so the model's output is bounded to known-good structures rather than open-ended, making results predictable and checkable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you still want to have uh, predictability of what the UI is going to be generated
